Definition: from a derivative of G4192; hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or influence, and thus differing from G2556, which refers rather to essential character, as well as from G4550, which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill, i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners:--bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness). See also G4191.
BiblicalUsage: Poneros is the word for evil that hurts, the evil one and the evil thing together. Jesus teaches us to pray for deliverance from evil, and warns that the wicked one snatches the seed sown in the heart. John says the whole world lies in wickedness, and Paul tells us to take up the shield of faith against the fiery darts of the wicked.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe evil is personal before it is abstract: there is a wicked one behind the wickedness, and he is real. But Christ has already overcome him, so I do not fight a battle whose outcome is in doubt.
